To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the identification of inference attacks on OLAP systems is a complex problem.
it is necessary to identify the possible attacks and their effects in the multidimensional data model.

the inference problem in data warehouses and OLAP systems can be identified and solved on the conceptual level and that the security of the system is increased by a combination of access and inference control.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the security level in an OLAP system? How do you evaluate the security level? How do you identify security holes in an OLAP application? How do you restrict or perturb the data?
the development of a security model for OLAP applications, which is independent of a specific database system and can be used for different applications.
a new approach for security control in multidimensional data warehouses and the development of a security analysis tool.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the security problem of OLAP applications is not only an access problem, but also an inference problem.

the problem is not to be solved by one of the mentioned techniques, but rather by the combination of several mechanisms, which are not only based on the database system itself but also on the application.
the security of OLAP applications is still an unsolved problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to identify and evaluate the inference problem of a multidimensional model.
we have identified the security problems in a data warehouse and we have shown that there are some solutions for these problems.
we have to identify security holes and to restrict access to data by aggregation, perturbation or other methods to avoid inference problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inference problem is a very complex issue and that there is no one-fits-all solution for all possible scenarios.
it is possible to identify security problems in a multidimensional data model.

the security of data warehouses can be improved by the identification and evaluation (e.g. with indicators) of possible attacks and by using the multidimensional model to control access and inferencing on the conceptual level.
